newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy war trial admits Jews as plaintiffs.
newsitem.headline: Italy war trial admits Jews as plaintiffs.

text.p: A military court trying former SS officers Erich Priebke and Karl Hass for their role in Italy's worst World War Two atrocity admitted Rome's Jewish Community to the case as a civil plaintiff on Thursday.

The community and an association of relatives of many of the 335 men and boys shot dead by SS forces in the 1944 massacre were granted plaintiff status after the court retired for more than four hours to consider their position.
Their admission had been opposed by lawyers for both defendants, neither of whom was in court, on grounds that the two associations had not been in existence at the time of the killings.
Civil plaintiff status will allow the two organisations to seek damages from the accused in the event of a guilty verdict.

Priebke, 83, and Hass, 84, are accused of complicity in multiple murder over the killings at the Ardeatine Caves south of Rome. Seventy-five of the victims, rounded up and shot in a reprisal for a partisan bomb attack on Nazi occupying forces, were Jews.
Priebke is being tried for the second time in the case after a controversial "guilty but not punishable" verdict at the end of his first trial last August was quashed on appeal.
The latest trial, at which Hass is a co-defendant for the first time, opened on Monday in the fortified courtroom of Rome's high-security Rebibbia jail.

Priebke, who is under house arrest at a Roman Catholic monastery south of Rome, and Hass have admitted to taking part in the 1944 massacre but argue that they were obliged to follow orders or face a firing squad.
Under Italian law, defendants are not obliged to attend trial sessions. The case continues.
